findings.description: `cleanup_old_files` uses `os.system(f"rm -rf {directory}/old/*")` with unsanitized input, allowing command injection via shell metacharacters in `directory`. Additionally, `rm -rf` can cause data loss if the resolved path is unexpected or maliciously crafted.

`run_backup` uses `subprocess.call(..., shell=True)` with an f-string interpolating `path` and `host`, allowing command injection. An attacker controlling these values can execute arbitrary shell commands.

`execute_command` passes user input directly to `os.popen(user_input)`, enabling arbitrary command execution. This is a direct command injection vulnerability and should not be used with untrusted input.

Use of `os.system`, `os.popen`, and `shell=True` are considered unsafe and deprecated practices. Prefer `subprocess.run` with a list of arguments and `shell=False`, and validate or sanitize all external inputs.
